57: /** Detect against a vocabulary containing these creature types / keywords. */
58: function signalsFor(
59:   row: CardRow,
60:   creatureTypes: string[] = [],
61:   keywords: string[] = [],
62: ): SignalMatch[] {
63:   const vocab = buildVocabulary(creatureTypes, keywords);
64:   return detectSignals(buildCardFacts(row, vocab), vocab);
65: }

67: function find(
68:   signals: SignalMatch[],
69:   archetype: string,
70:   qualifier?: string,
71: ): SignalMatch | undefined {
72:   return signals.find((s) => s.archetype === archetype && s.qualifier === qualifier);
73: }
74: 
75: function rolesOf(signals: SignalMatch[], archetype: string, qualifier?: string): Role[] {
76:   return (find(signals, archetype, qualifier)?.roles ?? []).slice().sort();
77: }

1: /**
2:  * The signal model: what a card contributes to a deck's plan, and in what
3:  * capacity.
4:  *
5:  * This replaces the old flat "theme" model, in which a signal was a single
6:  * regex applied identically to your card and to the candidate commander, and
7:  * two cards "synergised" when the same words appeared in both. That measured
8:  * lexical co-occurrence rather than synergy: "Sacrifice a creature" and
9:  * "Sacrifice Arid Mesa" are the same word and completely different mechanics,
10:  * and a commander that pays off a plan (Craterhoof Behemoth pumping your
11:  * board) usually shares no vocabulary at all with the cards that set it up.
12:  *
13:  * Three ideas do the work here.
14:  *
15:  * 1. ROLES. A card doesn't just "have" a theme, it participates in one in a
16:  *    particular capacity ΓÇö see `Role`. This is what lets one card carry
17:  *    several unrelated signals: Goblin Sharpshooter is Goblin kindred because
18:  *    of its creature *type*, and part of the creature-death cluster because of
19:  *    its *text*, and those two facts have nothing to do with each other.
20:  *
21:  * 2. TWO SIDES. Membership in a group is read off structured data wherever it
22:  *    exists (creature types, keywords, type line); qualifying as a *payoff*
23:  *    is read off rules text. A card's NAME is never evidence of anything ΓÇö
24:  *    see `stripSelfReferences` for why that mattered.
25:  *
26:  * 3. QUALIFIERS. A payoff can be restricted to a subtype, and then it only
27:  *    pays off cards of that subtype. Sliver Gravemother cares about Slivers
28:  *    in the graveyard, so it feeds "Reanimator (Sliver)" ΓÇö not generic
29:  *    Reanimator ΓÇö and every non-Sliver creature in your bin is worth nothing
30:  *    to it.
31:  *
32:  * Extending this: adding an archetype means adding one entry to `ARCHETYPES`
33:  * with per-role matchers. `Role`, `QualifierKind` and the catalog are all
34:  * meant to grow; nothing here is closed.
35:  */
36: import type { CardRow } from '../types';

38: /**
39:  * The capacity in which a card participates in an archetype.
40:  *
41:  * KNOWN LIMITATION ΓÇö this vocabulary is provisional and wants review. It
42:  * replaces an earlier "Outlet / Payoff" split that was reported as "not quite
43:  * right", and these five are an inference from worked examples rather than a
44:  * model anyone has signed off on. The specific problem with Outlet/Payoff was
45:  * that the two are almost never separable on a real card: Lathril's activated
46:  * ability *consumes* ten Elves and *rewards* you in the same breath, and
47:  * Viscera Seer is a sacrifice outlet whose whole point is the scry it gives
48:  * back. Splitting "consumes" from "rewards" lets one ability be both, which
49:  * Outlet/Payoff could not express.
50:  *
51:  * Cases known to still sit awkwardly:
52:  *  - Goblin Sharpshooter reads as `rewards` on creature-death here (it untaps
53:  *    when a creature dies), but it's often *described* as a sacrifice outlet,
54:  *    because with any outlet it becomes a machine gun. The card enables a
55:  *    loop it does not itself contain, and no role below captures "enables".
56:  *  - `is` on a vanilla creature is deliberately not wired into Aristocrats,
57:  *    even though a vanilla creature genuinely is sacrifice fodder ΓÇö counting
58:  *    it would make every creature deck read as Aristocrats.
59:  */
60: export type Role =
61:   /** The card *is* the resource: a Goblin, an Equipment, a land. Structured
62:    * data, never text. Passive ΓÇö see `ACTIVE_ROLES`. */
63:   | 'is'
64:   /** The card *makes* the resource: Goblin tokens, extra land drops, cards
65:    * into your own graveyard. */
66:   | 'produces'
67:   /** The card *needs* the resource, as a cost or a requirement: "Sacrifice a
68:    * creature:", "Tap ten untapped Elves:". */
69:   | 'consumes'
70:   /** The card *benefits* from the resource existing or the event happening:
71:    * Blood Artist, Craterhoof Behemoth, Teysa buffing your tokens. */
72:   | 'rewards'
73:   /** The card *doubles or repeats* the resource or event: Doubling Season,
74:    * Teysa making death triggers fire twice. A card that only amplifies needs
75:    * something else to amplify ΓÇö it generates no value alone. */
76:   | 'amplifies';
77: 
78: export const ROLES: Role[] = ['is', 'produces', 'consumes', 'rewards', 'amplifies'];

80: /**
81:  * Roles that mean the card actually engages with the plan, as opposed to
82:  * merely being a member of a group.
83:  *
84:  * This is the generalisation of the old "cares, not shares" kindred rule: a
85:  * commander needs at least one active role to be suggested for an archetype.
86:  * Silas Renn *is* a Human (`is`) and never mentions Humans, so he is not a
87:  * Human commander. Krenko *produces* Goblins and *rewards* having them, so he
88:  * is. The same test now covers keywords for free ΓÇö having Trample is `is`,
89:  * granting it to your team is `produces`.
90:  */
91: export const ACTIVE_ROLES: Role[] = ['produces', 'consumes', 'rewards', 'amplifies'];
92: 
93: export function hasActiveRole(roles: Role[]): boolean {
94:   return roles.some((r) => ACTIVE_ROLES.includes(r));
95: }

97: /** What a qualifier narrows a signal to. Open to growth ΓÇö card types and

143:   name: string;
144:   typeLine: string;
145:   /** Oracle text with the card's own name(s) removed. Match against this. */
146:   text: string;
147:   /** Oracle text as printed. Only for facts that need to see a self-reference,

150:   creatureTypes: string[];
151:   keywords: string[];
152:   /** Creature types this card creates tokens of. "Create two 1/1 red Goblin
153:    * creature tokens" makes Krenko's Command a Goblin card despite a Sorcery
154:    * having no creature types of its own. */
155:   producedTokenTypes: string[];
156:   /** The card sacrifices *itself* ΓÇö a fetch land, a Blood Crypt-style cost.
157:    * Distinct from sacrificing an indefinite object, which is the Aristocrats
158:    * pattern. */

161:   isCreature: boolean;

166: /**
167:  * Removes the card's own name from its oracle text.
168:  *
169:  * A card's rules text refers to itself by name, so any check that regexes a
170:  * word against oracle text will match that word for free when it appears in
171:  * the name. Goblin Sharpshooter's abilities are "doesn't untap", "whenever a
172:  * creature dies, untap" and a ping ΓÇö it does not care about Goblins in the
173:  * slightest ΓÇö yet it matched Goblin kindred purely because "Goblin" is in its
174:  * name. Names are not abilities, so they are removed before anything reads
175:  * the text.
176:  *
177:  * Both the full name and the pre-comma short form go, since rules text uses
178:  * the short form ("Lathril" for "Lathril, Blade of the Elves").
179:  */
180: export function stripSelfReferences(text: string, ...names: (string | null)[]): string {
181:   let out = text;
182:   const forms = new Set<string>();
183:   for (const name of names) {
184:     if (!name) continue;
185:     forms.add(name);
186:     // "Lathril, Blade of the Elves" -> also strip "Lathril".
187:     // .split() on any string always returns at least one element.
188:     const short = name.split(',')[0]!.trim();
189:     if (short && short !== name) forms.add(short);
190:   }
191:   // Longest first, so the full name goes before its own short form.
192:   for (const form of [...forms].sort((a, b) => b.length - a.length)) {
193:     out = out.split(form).join(' ');
194:   }
195:   return out;
196: }

198: function parseJsonArray(value: string | null): string[] {
199:   if (!value) return [];
200:   try {
201:     const parsed = JSON.parse(value);
202:     return Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed : [];
203:   } catch {
204:     return [];
205:   }
206: }

208: /** Every word in a piece of text, lowercased. The unit of vocabulary
209:  * lookup ΓÇö see `candidateTypes` for why looking up beats searching. */
210: function wordsIn(text: string): string[] {
211:   return text.toLowerCase().match(/[a-z][a-z'-]*/g) ?? [];
212: }
213: 
214: /**
215:  * Creature types of tokens this card creates.
216:  *
217:  * Read out of each "create ... token" clause, so a type mentioned elsewhere
218:  * in an unrelated sentence isn't credited as a token type.
219:  */
220: function findProducedTokenTypes(text: string, vocab: Vocabulary): string[] {
221:   const found = new Set<string>();
222:   for (const clause of text.match(/create[^.;]*token[^.;]*/gi) ?? []) {
223:     for (const word of wordsIn(clause)) {
224:       const type = vocab.typeByWord.get(word);
225:       if (type) found.add(type);
226:     }
227:   }
228:   return [...found];
229: }

231: /**
232:  * The creature types on a card, from its type line.
233:  *
234:  * Two filters, because either one alone lets junk through:
235:  *
236:  *   1. **Only Creature and Kindred cards have creature types** (CR 205.3m).
237:  *      Every other card type has its own subtype list. "Battle ΓÇö Control
238:  *      Point" made *Control* a creature type, so every card reading "creatures
239:  *      you control" was detected as caring about Control Kindred, and a real
240:  *      30-card list came back with a 14-card "Control Kindred" theme.
241:  *
242:  *   2. **The subtypes of a Creature card are still not all creature types.**
243:  *      They are mixed together and not positionally separable: "Artifact
244:  *      Creature ΓÇö Equipment Boar" and "Kindred Enchantment ΓÇö Lhurgoyf Aura"
245:  *      each carry one of each. That made Equipment, Aura, and Saga creature
246:  *      types, and produced a three-card "Aura Kindred" theme on a graveyard
247:  *      list.
248:  *
249:  * `knownTypes` is Scryfall's creature-type catalog, fetched alongside the bulk
250:  * data. Omitting it falls back to filter 1 only, which is what a database
251:  * seeded before the catalog existed gets ΓÇö narrower than nothing, and it
252:  * degrades rather than failing.
253:  */
254: export function parseCreatureTypes(typeLine: string, knownTypes?: Set<string>): string[] {
255:   const [typePart, subtypePart] = typeLine.split('ΓÇö');
256:   if (!subtypePart) return [];
257:   // typePart is always populated: .split() on any string returns at least
258:   // one element, which destructures into this position.
259:   // Word-boundary matched, and checked against the type part only: a Battle
260:   // whose subtype happened to read "Creature" would otherwise slip through.
261:   if (!/\b(Creature|Kindred|Tribal)\b/.test(typePart!)) return [];
262: 
263:   const words = subtypePart.trim().split(/\s+/).filter(Boolean);
264:   return knownTypes ? words.filter((word) => knownTypes.has(word)) : words;
265: }

267: /**
268:  * Lookup tables for the vocabulary signal detection recognises.
269:  *
270:  * Built once and reused across every card. The point is direction: with a
271:  * map, recognising a card's types costs one lookup per word it contains;
272:  * without one, it cost a regex per type in Magic. Across the card pool that
273:  * was the difference between ~8 seconds and ~82.
274:  */
275: export interface Vocabulary {
276:   /** Lowercased word, singular or plural, to its canonical creature type:
277:    * "elves" and "elf" both map to "Elf". */
278:   typeByWord: Map<string, string>;
279:   /** Lowercased single-word keyword to its canonical form. */
280:   keywordByWord: Map<string, string>;
281:   /** Keywords containing a space, which single-word lookup cannot find. */
282:   multiWordKeywords: string[];
283: }
284: 
285: export function buildVocabulary(creatureTypes: string[], keywords: string[]): Vocabulary {
286:   const typeByWord = new Map<string, string>();
287:   for (const type of creatureTypes) {
288:     typeByWord.set(type.toLowerCase(), type);
289:     typeByWord.set(pluralOfType(type).toLowerCase(), type);
290:   }
291: 
292:   const keywordByWord = new Map<string, string>();
293:   const multiWordKeywords: string[] = [];
294:   for (const keyword of keywords) {
295:     if (keyword.includes(' ')) multiWordKeywords.push(keyword);
296:     else keywordByWord.set(keyword.toLowerCase(), keyword);
297:   }
298: 
299:   return { typeByWord, keywordByWord, multiWordKeywords };
300: }

302: const wordPatternCache = new Map<string, RegExp>();
303: 
304: function escapeRegExp(value: string): string {
305:   return value.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
306: }
307: 
308: /**
309:  * The English plural of a creature type, because cards refer to a type in the
310:  * aggregate ΓÇö "Elves you control", not "Elf you control". Only the irregular
311:  * endings Magic's type list actually contains are handled.
312:  */
313: export function pluralOfType(type: string): string {
314:   // Elf -> Elves, Dwarf -> Dwarves. Lathril says "ten untapped Elves you
315:   // control", so missing this drops one of the format's best-known kindred
316:   // commanders.
317:   if (/f$/i.test(type)) return type.replace(/f$/i, 'ves');
318:   // Sphinx -> Sphinxes, Fungus -> Funguses, Leech -> Leeches.
319:   if (/(s|x|z|ch|sh)$/i.test(type)) return `${type}es`;
320:   return `${type}s`;
321: }
322: 
323: const tokenDescriptorCache = new Map<string, RegExp>();
324: 
325: /**
326:  * A token's printed type line inside a "create" clause ΓÇö "Goblin creature
327:  * tokens", "Elf Warrior creature tokens". One optional intervening word so a
328:  * token with two creature types still matches.
329:  */
330: function tokenDescriptorPattern(type: string): RegExp {
331:   let pattern = tokenDescriptorCache.get(type);
332:   if (!pattern) {
333:     const forms = `(?:${escapeRegExp(type)}|${escapeRegExp(pluralOfType(type))})`;
334:     pattern = new RegExp(`\\b${forms}(?:\\s+\\w+)?\\s+(?:creature\\s+)?tokens?\\b`, 'gi');
335:     tokenDescriptorCache.set(type, pattern);
336:   }
337:   // Shared cached regex with /g ΓÇö reset before each use.
338:   pattern.lastIndex = 0;
339:   return pattern;
340: }
341: 
342: /** Matches a word or its plural, on a word boundary. Cached: this runs against
343:  * every candidate in a pool of thousands. */
344: function wordPattern(word: string): RegExp {
345:   let pattern = wordPatternCache.get(word);
346:   if (!pattern) {
347:     pattern = new RegExp(
348:       `\\b(?:${escapeRegExp(word)}|${escapeRegExp(pluralOfType(word))})\\b`,
349:       'i',
350:     );
351:     wordPatternCache.set(word, pattern);
352:   }
353:   return pattern;
354: }

356: /**
357:  * Whether the card sacrifices *itself*, as opposed to an indefinite object.
358:  *
359:  * Two spellings, because Scryfall changed theirs. Older text named the card
360:  * ("Sacrifice Arid Mesa:"); current text says "Sacrifice this land:" /
361:  * "Sacrifice this creature:". Both are read off the RAW text ΓÇö the
362:  * name-stripped copy renders the first form as a bare "Sacrifice :".
363:  */
364: function detectsSelfSacrifice(rawText: string, name: string): boolean {
365:   if (/\bsacrifice this\b/i.test(rawText)) return true;
366:   // .split() on any string always returns at least one element.
367:   const short = name.split(',')[0]!.trim();
368:   if (!short) return false;
369:   return new RegExp(`sacrifice ${escapeRegExp(short)}\\b`, 'i').test(rawText);
370: }

372: /**
373:  * Removes reminder text ΓÇö the parenthetical restatement of a keyword.
374:  *
375:  * Reminder text explains a keyword the card already has; it is never an
376:  * ability of its own. Leaving it in produced real false positives: Sliver
377:  * Gravemother's Encore reminder text ends "They gain haste", which read as
378:  * the card *granting* haste to your team, i.e. an active Haste payoff.
379:  */
380: function stripReminderText(text: string): string {
381:   return text.replace(/\([^)]*\)/g, ' ');
382: }

384: export function buildCardFacts(row: CardRow, vocab: Vocabulary): CardFacts {
385:   const rawText = row.oracle_text ?? '';
386:   const text = stripReminderText(stripSelfReferences(rawText, row.name, row.back_name ?? null));
387:   const typeLine = row.type_line ?? '';
388:   return {
389:     name: row.name,
390:     typeLine,
391:     text,
392:     rawText,
393:     creatureTypes: parseJsonArray(row.creature_types),
394:     keywords: parseJsonArray(row.keywords),
395:     producedTokenTypes: findProducedTokenTypes(text, vocab),
396:     sacrificesItself: detectsSelfSacrifice(rawText, row.name),
397:     isLand: /\bLand\b/.test(typeLine),
398:     isCreature: /\bCreature\b/.test(typeLine),
399:     isEquipment: /\bEquipment\b/.test(typeLine),
400:     isAura: /\bAura\b/.test(typeLine),
401:   };
402: }
